patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..732136e 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -1,11 +1,10 @@
-from store import CUSTOMERS, ORDERS
+from store import ORDERS
 
 
 def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Baseline run_tests.py -> 'visible tests passed' (shipped tests do not catch the bug). 2) Reproduced: report dump showed 101/102 each appearing twice, a@acme.test seeing b@acme.test's order, total 290. 3) Applied fix. 4) run_tests.py -> passed. 5) Re-dumped report: each order exactly once, total 165. 6) git status --porcelain shows only queries.py modified.
cause: orders_for_customer matched by name instead of unique id; two customers named Acme each received both customers' orders, duplicating lines and inflating the total. Fix ties each order to its true owner via customer_id.
